Stablecoin routing

Explained

Business international payments, explained

Key points

  • A cross-border payment is money sent from one country to another, usually with a currency conversion along the way.
  • You see what your recipient gets before you confirm.
  • With stablecoin routing, your recipient still receives an ordinary currency.

What is a cross-border payment?

A cross-border payment is money sent from one country to another, usually with a currency conversion along the way. Paying a supplier abroad, sending money to family and receiving a salary from another country are all cross-border payments.

Where stablecoins come in

When you send, Ibanora converts your money into a USD stablecoin, moves it across the border and converts it into the recipient’s currency. Neither of you needs a crypto wallet, because both ends of the payment are ordinary currencies.

What are B2B international payments?

B2B international payments are payments between businesses in different countries, such as paying a supplier abroad or collecting from an overseas customer. A business can pay suppliers, contractors and staff abroad from the balance it already holds, and collect from customers in other countries. Each payment keeps its reference, which makes matching it to an invoice simpler. See business accounts.

Ways to make an international payment

There are several common ways to move money between countries:

  • SWIFT transfers: banks send the payment instruction to each other over the SWIFT network, and the money may pass through one or more intermediary (correspondent) banks.
  • SEPA transfers: euro payments between countries in the Single Euro Payments Area, which includes the EU and several other European countries.
  • Local transfers through a provider: a payment provider pays the recipient from within their own country, in their currency.
  • Stablecoin routing: the value is carried as a stablecoin in the middle, and each end stays in an ordinary currency. This is how Ibanora routes cross-border payments.

What an international payment costs

The cost of an international payment can include the exchange-rate margin (the difference between the rate you get and the mid-market rate), a transfer fee, fees taken by intermediary banks along the way and a fee charged by the receiving bank.

A simple way to compare quotes is the amount your recipient gets for the same amount sent. Before you confirm an Ibanora payment, you see both amounts. Ask whether the recipient’s bank may also charge a fee.

What you see before you send

Before you confirm, you see the amount you send and the amount your recipient gets. Then you can follow the payment as it is sent, converted and delivered. You can pay from a euro, USD or GBP balance.

Cross-border payment questions

Where can I send money?

The countries and currencies open to you depend on your own country and verification. Services are provided through our partner Mosta. Contact us about a specific destination.

How long does a payment take?

It depends on the currencies and countries involved. You can follow each payment in your account until it is delivered.

What does a payment cost?

Pricing depends on your country, the currencies and the amount. You see what your recipient gets before you confirm. Talk to us for details.

Does my recipient need a stablecoin wallet?

No. The stablecoin step happens in between, and your recipient receives an ordinary currency.

Can I send stablecoins directly?

Yes, from a stablecoin wallet to a wallet address you enter. To turn stablecoins into money in a bank account, use the off-ramp.

Do I need a separate account for international payments?

No. You can pay from the EUR, USD, GBP or other balance you already hold in your Ibanora account, depending on your country and verification. See business accounts. If you are comparing providers, our guide to Wise alternatives covers some of the options.

Who provides the payment service?

Payment services are provided through our partner Mosta. Ibanora is a technology brand and not a bank. See the disclaimer.
